rules.title: Context minimalism
rules.what: Give the model the goal, the constraints and a path to the details (files, search, tools) - not the content itself.
rules.why: Prompt context is processed on every exchange of the turn: tokens processed cost computation, and computation costs energy. Bloat also degrades attention on what matters.
rules.how: State the goal in a short brief; let the model read files with read_file/grep instead of pasting them; use @ mentions for the few files that matter.

verify.how: Input token count of the prompt is proportionate to the task.

limits: Direction (fewer tokens -> less compute -> less energy) holds; any token-to-watts ratio depends on caching, model, hardware - measure before quoting numbers.

rules.title: Ask the one question that changes the work
rules.what: Ask a blocking question only when a wrong assumption would reshape the work; otherwise state the assumption and proceed.
rules.why: A round trip costs a full model exchange; four questions where one mattered pays three times for nothing. But the one question that changes the architecture is the cheapest exchange of the project.
rules.how: Name the assumption that would reshape the task. Genuinely ambiguous - ask and wait. Otherwise - state it in one line and build.

verify.how: Prompts carry stated assumptions rather than open questions the repository could answer.

rules.title: Let the model fetch on demand
rules.what: The model has read_file, grep and search tools: give pointers, not payloads.
rules.why: Details fetched on demand are processed once, when needed, at exactly the relevant granularity. Details pasted are processed again on every subsequent exchange of the session.
rules.how: File paths and search keywords in the prompt; the model pulls what it needs and keeps the rest out of context.

verify.how: Session input tokens measured against the alternative (pasted content) for the same result.

rules.title: Compact instead of dragging history
rules.what: In a long session, /compact the context (or start a new session with a short brief) rather than carrying the entire history through every exchange.
rules.why: Long histories are re-processed at each exchange; compaction keeps the intents and drops the noise, at a fraction of the tokens.
rules.how: After large milestones, /compact; for a new task, /clear or a fresh session with a written summary of what matters.

verify.how: Session context size stays within the model's efficient range rather than growing monotonically.

limits: Compaction loses detail; keep decisions in files (docs, decisions.md) the session can re-read.

rules.title: Right model for the task
rules.what: Route the task to the smallest model that meets the quality bar: /model switches; mechanical work does not need the large model.
rules.why: Inference cost scales with model size across every exchange; a large model on a mechanical task pays the difference for identical output.
rules.how: Large model for design, hard debugging, architecture; smaller for mechanical refactors, format conversions, doc chores. /thinking levels likewise.

verify.how: Task quality equal on a sample; cost per task lower.

limits: The quality bar is the user's call; the rule forces the deliberate choice, not the smallest by default.

rules.title: Deterministic tools before model reasoning
rules.what: Prefer a deterministic tool (grep, a script, a linter, a validator) over model reasoning for anything a tool decides as well.
rules.why: A grep result is exact, cheap and reproducible; the same question answered by generation pays reasoning tokens for a possibly-wrong answer.
rules.how: Run the script/linter/grep and give the model the output; the model interprets results, it does not emulate tools.

verify.how: Deterministic checks (tests, linters, this skill's audit) back the statements made about the code.

rules.title: One turn, one goal
rules.what: Each prompt pursues one goal; sprawled mega-prompts produce half-done work that needs re-runs.
rules.why: A re-run costs the whole exchange again; work done once at the right granularity is the cheapest. Focus also improves output quality.
rules.how: Split the work into goal-sized prompts; queue follow-ups while the agent runs (the input queue exists for that).

verify.how: Turns end with the goal met or a clear blocker, not with diffuse partial output.

rules.title: No blind retries
rules.what: Retry with new information, not with the same prompt: an unchanged retry re-pays the exchange for the same result.
rules.why: A retry that varies nothing is the purest waste: same input, same output, same cost. What changes is what you add (a detail, a constraint, a correction).
rules.how: On failure, say what was missing or wrong in the previous attempt; /retry with additional instructions carries the correction.

verify.how: Retried prompts carry an explicit change from the failed attempt.

rules.title: Reuse validated artifacts
rules.what: When a validated artifact exists (a script, a patch, a document), reference it rather than asking the model to regenerate it.
rules.why: Regenerating what exists re-pays generation for a possibly-different result, and reintroduces defects the artifact had already shed.
rules.how: Keep validated outputs as files; the model edits them rather than re-authoring them.

verify.how: Requests target existing artifacts (edit) before creating new ones (generate).

rules.title: Subagents keep the main context clean
rules.what: Delegate exploration and broad scans to subagents; keep the main session for the work that needs the full picture.
rules.why: A subagent's exploratory context (grep results, file dumps) is summarised back, not carried: the main session pays for the conclusion, not the search.
rules.how: spawn a subagent for 'explore the codebase and report the call sites' style work; the main session keeps its context for design and edits.

verify.how: Main-session context growth measured with vs without delegated exploration.

limits: Coordination overhead; delegate bounded, well-scoped explorations.

rules.title: Images only when they carry the task
rules.what: Attach images only when the pixels carry information (screenshots, designs, diagrams); text carries everything else.
rules.why: Vision processing costs multiples of text per unit of information; a task that can be described in three lines does not need a screenshot.
rules.how: Describe in text what text can carry; use images for visual state (UI bugs, design references, error dialogs).

verify.how: Each attached image has a stated purpose the text could not carry.

rules.title: Close what you opened
rules.what: Stop background processes, servers and watchers when done; exit sessions instead of leaving them resident.
rules.why: A forgotten dev server or watcher burns CPU watching a directory nobody is changing.
rules.how: The background process list is checked and stopped at session end; servers run when someone uses them.

verify.how: No orphaned background processes from the session (process list clean).

rules.title: Batch related work in the queue
rules.what: Queue related follow-up prompts while the agent runs (they merge into one turn) instead of serial ping-pong.
rules.why: Queued prompts delivered together share one turn's context processing; sequential ones each re-pay the whole exchange.
rules.how: Write follow-ups as they occur and submit them into the input queue; review the merged turn's output once.

verify.how: Turns per milestone measured; related corrections grouped.

rules.title: Verify before you regenerate
rules.what: Run the tests/linters before asking the model to 'try again' - the failure may not be in the generated code at all.
rules.why: A regeneration based on an unverified hypothesis re-pays generation for a defect that one test run would have localised.
rules.how: On a failing result: run the check, read the error, give the model the precise failure. /retry with the actual error message beats /retry with 'still broken'.

verify.how: Retry prompts cite the actual error output.

rules.title: Automation proportional to need
rules.what: Hooks and scheduled automation run proportional checks: audit the diff, not the whole repository on every write; schedule heavy scans, not per-keystroke ones.
rules.why: A hook that re-scans everything on every edit multiplies audit cost by edit count; a diff-scoped hook pays only for what changed.
rules.how: Scope hooks to the changed content (this skill's post-edit hook does), set timeouts, keep scheduled jobs at a justified interval.

verify.how: Hook runtime per tool call within its timeout budget; scan scope matches the change.

rules.title: Directions, not ratios
rules.what: When discussing the agent's own footprint: state the direction (fewer tokens -> less compute -> less energy), refuse the ratio (tokens to watts/CO2 without measurement).
rules.why: Prompt caching, model size, batching, hardware and grid mix each move the token-to-energy result more than the token count. A quoted ratio without measurement is a fabricated number.
rules.how: Reduce because the computation is real; before quoting any energy figure, measure the actual workload on the actual hardware.

verify.how: No token-to-energy conversion appears without a cited measurement.
